title.narrative: Somalia Recurrent Cost & Reform Financing Project - Phase 2

description.narrative: The development objective of the Second Phase of the Recurrent Cost and Reform Financing Project for Somalia is to enable the Somali Government to achieve reliable and transparent financing of critical civil service operations to help strengthen the legitimacy of the state. The project comprises of four components. The first component, support to core government functions of ministries, departments, and agencies (MDAs) in Federal Government of Somalia (FGS) will finance: the salaries of eligible non-security sector civil servants in the MDAs; the cost of staff injected under the capacity injection mechanism (CIM); and non-salary operating costs for MDAs. It consists of following three sub-components: (i) financing of eligible civil service salaries in non-security sectors in FGS; (ii) financing of salaries and allowances to government staff and young graduates recruited under the capacity injection mechanism (CIM) in FGS; and (iii) financing of eligible non-salary recurrent costs in MDA in the FGS. The second component is inter-governmental fiscal transfers to core government functions of eligible federal member states, interim, and emerging administrations. It consists of following two sub-components: (i) transfers to interim and emerging states for core government functions; and (ii) inter-governmental fora on transfers and information exchanges. The third component, support of recurrent costs in health and education sectors in FGS and eligible member states, interim, and emerging administrations will support the FGS, Puntland, and interim Jubba administration (IJA) to expand their service delivery systems through improvement of accountability systems and support of recurrent costs in the education and health sectors. The fourth component, project management and coordination will support coordination, administration, communication, management, procurement, monitoring and evaluation (M and E), as well as impact-evaluation, auditing, and dissemination of project activities in FGS, Puntland, and the IJA.

To support the Federal Government of Somalia and Eligible Federal Member States to strengthen resource management systems, the inter-governmental fiscal framework, and service delivery systems in health and education.

baseline.value: 2018 fiscal transfers to FMS budgeted at USD 12m, with USD 5.4m for block transfers under Ministry of Interior and Federal Affairs

comment.narrative: <p>DLI not fully met a similar indicator was included in RCRF III</p>

actual.value: Not met for 2021. Execution rate for fiscal transfers to FMS for the months (Jan-June) of 2021 is 18.48%, (US$10.45m/56.5million) which is less than the outturn rate for domestic revenue of 37.1%, (US$100million/$269.7million)

comment.narrative: <p>Target reached. Total transfers to eligible FMS by end of 2019 were US$27.3 million or 81% compared to the baseline year of 2018(US$15 million). Total transfers to eligible FMS by end of 2020 were US$59.6 million or 296% compared to the baseline year of 2018 (US$15 million). Total transfers to eligible FMS in the FY2021 were US$31.6 million or 109.9% compared to the baseline. Despite the decline of 47% compared to FY2020, the target has been achieved.</p>

title.narrative: Women of child bearing age (15-59 years) and children 0-59 months referred to health facilities by Female Health Workers

comment.narrative: <p>Referrals were made as follows: BRA (16 %), GSS (8 %), HSS (33 %), JSS (22%),PSS 3.%, SWS 68% which was an average of 25%.</p>

title.narrative: Eligible FMS/BRA conducting proficiency testing of teachers as an annual exercise establishing minimum competency level of teachers (DLI 7)

comment.narrative: <p>Target reached. Proficiency test exercise in four FMS/BRA (Banadir Regional Administration) was conducted in 2020.</p>

title.narrative: Female Health Workers selected according to guidelines, trained, and actively providing services

comment.narrative: <p>In addition to the existing 340 FHWs and 19 FHSs in Puntland, Galmudug, and BRA, 546 new FHWs and 39 FHSs were recruited and trained and are actively delivering services in all eligible FMS and BRA.</p>

<p>Target reached. Five technical meetings took place in the past 12 months (FY2022) – Inter-Governmental Fiscal Federalism Technical Working Group (IGFFC TWG) in Garowe, June 2021, Inter-Governmental Fiscal Federalism Technical Commitee (IGFFTC) in Nairobi, October 2021, IGFFTC in Addis Ababa, January 2022 and June 2022, IGC on Education in Kismayo, December 2021.</p>

title.narrative: Monthly payroll reports published on MOF website

comment.narrative: <p>Target reached. Fiscal reports for January–December 2021 and January–April 2022 were published on the Ministry of Finance (MOF) website on time</p>

title.narrative: Share of civil servants' salaries financed by government

comment.narrative: <p>Target reached. Total amount of civil service wage bill financed by the FGS budget was 86% in January–December 2021. In previous ISRs, the value represented the total amount of civil servants’ salaries deducted by the amount of ‘baseline’ civil service salaries and CIM (Capacity Injection Mechanism) salaries paid by the RCRF and divided by the total amount of non-security sector civil servants’ salaries. The value does not include the DLI amounts. If DLI disbursements are to be added, the indicator value changes to 53 percent in 2019, 66 % in 2020, 34 percent in 2021, and 45 percent in FY2022 (July 2021–June 2022).</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of eligible civil servants salaries paid on time

comment.narrative: <p>Target reached. Ready for payment with the Central Bank of Somalia (CBS) or the commercial bank between the government statutorypay period of 25th and 28th of the month. Nine months’ salary paid on and before the statutory date, 28th of each month. March, April, and May salaries were paid after the statutory date</p>

title.narrative: Strengthened payment process for operational expenditures (DLI 4) (Percent)

baseline.value: Cash advances to MDAs 50% of operating expenditures.

actual.value: All government payments for salaries, transfers and capital expenditures to be executed as payments to Bank accounts directly to vendors, with the exception of: petty cash, travel advances, security sector and contingency (per Appropriation Act)

baseline.value: Lack of a coherent system for school supervision, with inadequate financing to enable FMS education ministries to fulfil this function

comment.narrative: <p>School supervision exercise conducted in five states (PSS, HSS, GSS, JSS, and SWSS) and Benadir region in April–May 2022. The reports are in draft status and will be shared by June 30, 2022.</p>

actual.value: School supervision reports for the period of November 2019 to April 2020 covering 1,554 primary and secondary schools were preparedfor five states (PSS, HSS, GSS, JSS, and SWSS) and Benadir region. No school supervision was conducted in 2021 due to COVID-relatedschool closures.

title.narrative: Contract Management Unit established and fully staffed according to organogram

comment.narrative: <p>Contract management and M&E specialists along with health focal points were successfully hired at the FGS MoH and four FMS MoHs in FY2022</p>
